test_title: PYST 54: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 11 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Consider a triangle PQR, right-angled at R, in which PQ = 29 units, QR = 21 units, and ∠PQR = θ. Find the value of cos²θ - sin²θ.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the known Pythagorean triplet (20, 21, 29).

Since Hypotenuse = 29 and Base = 21, the Perpendicular must be 20.

cosθ = Base / Hypotenuse = 21/29 and sinθ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse = 20/29.

cos²θ − sin²θ = (21² − 20²) / 29² = (441 − 400) / 841 = 41/841.

**∴ The correct answer is 41/841.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔPQR, ∠R = 90° and ∠PQR = θ

⇒ Hypotenuse PQ = 29 units

⇒ Base QR = 21 units

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc73f6253fa1ae956c8ccf0e632384d9dc656e0717b8b10734af3e4313e6f129.png] 

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Pythagoras Theorem: Perpendicular² + Base² = Hypotenuse²

⇒ cosθ = Base / Hypotenuse

⇒ sinθ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

⇒ PR² + QR² = PQ²

⇒ PR² + 21² = 29²

⇒ PR² + 441 = 841

⇒ PR² = 841 − 441 = 400

⇒ PR = √400 = 20 units (Perpendicular for ∠Q)

⇒ cosθ = 21 / 29

⇒ sinθ = 20 / 29

Now, calculate cos²θ − sin²θ:

⇒ (21 / 29)² − (20 / 29)²

⇒ (441 / 841) − (400 / 841)

⇒ (441 − 400) / 841

⇒ 41 / 841

**∴ The correct answer is 41/841.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Perpendicular² + Base² = Hypotenuse².

Double Angle Formula

The expression cos²θ − sin²θ is geometrically equivalent to the double angle formula for cosine, which is cos(2θ).

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Useful combinations of integers that satisfy the Pythagoras theorem include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (20, 21, 29).
